title: The source file is named v2 while its metadata table gives Version 1, and it carries no change-log row
section: Metadata table, rows Version and Date; there is no change-log section
description: The file is named v2 and dated 28 October 2026, while its metadata table gives Version 1 at the same date and the document has no change log. Version 3 is issued next to the file, the Supersedes row records the version the file name carries, and the change log records the source as row 1 because no row 2 exists.
evidence: File name 'Recovery Workbench Test Strategy v2.docx'; metadata table rows '| Version | 1 |' and '| Date | 28 October 2026 |'; the document ends at section 7 Defects and contains no change-log table.
proposed: Confirm whether the source carries version 1 or version 2, add the missing change-log row, and keep the file name and the metadata table in step from the next version on.

title: No approval of the new version is recorded and the source has no Status row
section: Metadata table; the document carries no approval or sign-off section
description: The source has no status row and no approval record. The realignment run takes no approval stop, so version 3 carries Status Draft and the opening note states that no approval is recorded.
evidence: The v2 metadata table has five rows only: Document, Version, Date, Prepared by and Structure. The document contains no approval, sign-off or status statement and ends at section 7 Defects.
proposed: Record the approval of version 3 by the test lead and the programme, with a date, and add a Status row with the approver role to the metadata table of every later version.

title: The nine levels of version 2 describe one deployable and state no criteria for contract, component or wave integration testing
source: Recovery Workbench Test Strategy v2; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1
description: Version 2 has nine levels written for modules in one deployable with one schema and one API base: Integration means modules with a real PostgreSQL database and API contract means requests and responses against one OpenAPI file. The realignment needs a contract level for three contract shapes, a component level against fakes, and one integration test group per wave. The rows are added with who runs them, where and when, taken from Architecture v5 slides 11 and 46 and Template and Rules section R5.4; no source states their exit criteria, so the criteria written in the new rows are an assumption.
evidence: Version 2 section 1: nine rows, Integration described as 'Modules with a real PostgreSQL database' and API contract as 'Requests and responses against the OpenAPI file'. Architecture v5 slide 11 gives five call types with one contract each (OpenAPI 3.1, AsyncAPI 3.0, contract jar, file manifest, SQL views); slide 46 states contract tests per API, event and activity, Temporal replay tests and Testcontainers; Template and Rules R5.4 allows an I dependency on ITG stories only and R5.1 gives the integration epics RWB-ITG-W1 to RWB-ITG-W4.
proposed: Confirm the exit criteria of the Contract, Component and integration-test-group levels and carry them into the Definition of Ready and Done, so that a story's Done and the level's exit agree.

title: No source names the owner of a contract test or of a contract fake
source: Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1; Recovery Workbench Test Strategy v2
section: Section 5 Who tests what; sections 8 and 9
description: The Ownership Map fixes the owner of every table, REST operation, event, workflow and job, but it names no test owner, and no source states who keeps a contract fake. Version 3 reads the test owner and the fake owner from the contract owner in the map: the service that publishes a contract owns its contract test and its fake.
evidence: Ownership Map v1 sheets Tables, Endpoints, Events, Workflows and activities, Jobs and Parameters give one owner code per item and hold no test column; version 2 section 5 names team types only: Developers, QA engineers, business testers, SCB IT security and role owners.
proposed: Confirm that the owning service keeps the contract test and the fake of every contract it publishes, and state it in the Definition of Ready and Done and in the story template.

title: How SIT is composed while a later-wave service does not exist is not stated
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Test Strategy v2
section: Section 2 Environments; section 10 Integration test group per wave
description: Services arrive in waves of 9, 4, 4 and 2, so in SIT during a wave some Recovery services do not exist yet. Version 3 states that the services of the wave under test run for real, that a fake never stands in for a service that exists in SIT, and that a later wave's published contract is served by its fake. No source states how SIT is composed across waves.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 38 gives the wave contents (Wave 1: nine services; Wave 2: P8, S2, S5, S8; Wave 3: S1, S3, S4, S6; Wave 4: S7, S9); Template and Rules R5.6 gives the wave map; version 2 section 2 names three environments and does not discuss a partly deployed Workbench.
proposed: Confirm how SIT is composed for each wave: which services are deployed, which contracts are served by a fake, and how the fake is withdrawn when the owning service arrives.

title: The environments are counted but never named in any source
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Test Strategy v2
description: Architecture v5 counts 19 x 4 environments and names none of them. Version 2 names DEV, SIT and UAT. Version 3 keeps the three environments the source names and does not name the fourth, which the count implies.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 45 answer: 'One cluster per service would be 19 x 4 environments'; slide 34 gives one Temporal cluster per environment and names no environment. Version 2 section 2: three rows, DEV, SIT and UAT.
proposed: Publish the name, purpose and data rule of each of the four environments per service, so that every test level names the environment it runs in.

title: The journey steps and test cases of each wave are not stated
source: Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1
section: Section 10 Integration test group per wave
description: The integration epics, the harness and the four journey stories exist (RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG, RWB-ITG-W1J02-ITG, RWB-ITG-W2J01-ITG, RWB-ITG-W3J01-ITG and RWB-ITG-W4J01-ITG), and version 3 states what each wave journey proves. The step-by-step journey and its test case IDs are not stated in any source read for this document.
evidence: Template and Rules R5.1 gives the integration epics RWB-ITG-W1 to RWB-ITG-W4 and RWB-ITG-NFR; R5.7 makes the harness W1J01 Day 1; R7.2 section 16 rules that an ITG copy of a test case ends in -ITG. The Change Register v1 gives the five ITG stories with their IDs and no journey steps. Architecture v5 slides 42 and 43 give the events, not the journey steps.
proposed: Write the step-by-step journey and the test case IDs of each wave in its journey story, so that a wave gate can be signed against a named list.

title: The Ownership Map assigns no table to rwb-valuation although Architecture v5 gives it a schema
source: Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1
section: Section 11 Test scope per service, row S1
description: The map assigns zero tables to S1 rwb-valuation, while Architecture v5 slide 18 gives the service the schema rwb_valuation with valuations, the D6 route decision and the route agent output. Version 3 states the counts as the map gives them and records that the data level of S1 cannot be tested until the tables are assigned.
evidence: Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables holds no row owned by S1 (owner counts: S1 0, S2 1, S3 1, S4 2, S5 2, S6 2, S7 1, S8 1, S9 3). Architecture v5 slide 18, S1 OUT: 'schema rwb_valuation (valuations, D6 route decision, route agent output)'.
proposed: Assign the rwb_valuation tables in the Ownership Map and the Physical Schema folder, so that the component and integration tests of S1 have a schema to seed and assert on.
